evals.name: full-triage
evals.prompt: Run the substrate audit against https://pod.vardeman.me/vault/ and go through whatever it flags — for each finding, work out the fix and draft proposals I can review.
evals.expected_output: Runs pod-audit (or equivalent discovery), triages each of the ~11 findings, classifies by mem:stalenessClass, resolves against ground truth, and drafts mem:RealignAction proposals to working/curator-proposals/ (saved to output dir). Reports per-finding class + repair direction + proposal location.
assertions: Obtained the work queue by running the substrate audit (pod_audit.py / make audit) rather than guessing findings
Triaged all three finding clusters: stale rdfs:seeAlso, missing entry-point sh:agentInstruction, and the 8 untyped addressbook descriptors
Classified findings using mem:stalenessClass values (e.g. mem:DanglingReference)
Drafted proposals as mem:RealignAction with a required mem:rationale
Routed proposals to /vault/wiki/working/curator-proposals/ (two-stage commit) — did not edit affected resources directly
Did not modify or delete any existing substrate resource (safety constraint honored)

evals.name: stale-references
evals.prompt: I renamed some wiki containers a while back — pages became concepts and sources got merged in. I'm pretty sure something on the Pod still points at the old paths. Find what's stale and draft repairs.
evals.expected_output: Finds the stale rdfs:seeAlso pointers (wiki/pages/, wiki/sources/) in the storage description, classifies as mem:DanglingReference, recognizes the static void-description.json (repo) as the source rather than a PATCHable resource, and drafts a repair recommendation. Does not name the audit tool in the prompt.
assertions: Identified BOTH stale pointers (wiki/pages/ and wiki/sources/) as the rename casualties
Resolved against ground truth (confirmed live container set / Type Index routing to concepts/)
Recognized the fix is repo-side in void-description.json (storage description not HTTP-PATCHable, 405) rather than proposing an N3 Patch to the Pod
Classified the stale pointers (mem:DanglingReference / SupersededConcept)
Drafted a repair proposal or recommendation with recorded reasoning

evals.name: contract-gap
evals.prompt: Those addressbook contact affordances (contact-find-by-name etc.) look half-finished next to wiki-search-grep. Check whether they're properly described as affordance descriptors, and if not, propose fixes.
evals.expected_output: Detects the 8 addressbook descriptors are typed wiki:Affordance only (no prof:ResourceDescriptor / role / label / conformsTo / installedBy), recognizes this as a contract gap, and constructs the missing predicates as proposals (composed from what each descriptor already does).
assertions: Detected the 8 addressbook descriptors are typed wiki:Affordance only and lack prof:ResourceDescriptor
Named the missing contract predicates (prof:hasRole, rdfs:label, dct:conformsTo, wiki:installedBy)
Constructed a fix adding the missing predicates, composed from what each descriptor already does
Preserved the existing working sh:agentInstruction + wiki:selectQuery
Made the correct subtype judgment: did NOT add wiki:SearchAffordance/dispatchPattern (these are SPARQL SELECT, not HTTP ?ext= dispatch)

evals.name: false-positive-guard
evals.prompt: My notes say the Pod has an '8-shape catalog' but I count 11 shape files — that's a bug, clean it up.
evals.expected_output: Applies the false-positive guard: dereferences the canonical decision (D98), finds it reconciles ('8 SHACL NodeShapes / 11 shape files total'), determines the claim is correct, and WITHDRAWS the flag (records as mem:FalsePositive) rather than rewriting a correct-at-its-granularity statement. The discriminating test.
assertions: Dereferenced the canonical decision (D98) rather than acting on the surface count claim
Concluded it is NOT a bug — the 8 NodeShapes vs 11 files reconcile
Withdrew the flag (recorded as mem:FalsePositive) instead of rewriting the correct claim
Did not make any damaging edit to the correct statement
